head: claude/ranking-key-ab-dies-instantly-on-every-push
title: file: ranking-key-ab.yml concludes failure instantly on every push, main included
body:
One backlog row. **Filed, not fixed** — lanes are paused by operator directive and filing is the act of not taking the item.

_Opened via the `pr-opener` relay: `mcp__github__create_pull_request` returned HTTP 500 twice, and a check for a partially-created PR came back empty._

### What I saw
While reading `actions_list` to check CI on my own PR #12219 during the close-out, `.github/workflows/ranking-key-ab.yml` showed `conclusion: failure` on both of my heads. That could have been mine, so I ran the base-branch control rather than assuming: it fails on **`main`** too.

**Population, because it bounds the claim:** the 5 most recent runs on `main` (run numbers 2814, 2836, 2839, 2917, 2919) plus the 2 on my branch (2920, 2923). **All seven `failure`.**

**The shape is the diagnostic:** every one has `created_at == updated_at == run_started_at` to the second — e.g. run `34747542844`, all three `2026-09-13T08:22:59Z`. A run that starts and finishes inside one second executed no job body, so this is a startup/workflow-level failure, not a test or guard failing.

### What I did not establish, said plainly
- **I did not read the cause.** No workflow file opened, no run log. The specific defect is unknown and deliberately not guessed at — a startup failure has several causes with different fixes.
- **I read 7 of 224 runs.** The lifetime failure rate is unmeasured, and "it has never worked" is *not* claimed.

### Why it matters
It is **not a required check** — absent from `get_check_runs` on #12219 — so it blocks no PR and pages nobody. That is almost certainly why it has gone unremarked, and it is the finding rather than a mitigation: a workflow failing instantly on every push is indistinguishable, on every surface a human reads, from one that works.

### On the near-duplicate
`append_row` flagged `BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING` at 0.67 overlap. I read it: **not a duplicate and not a recurrence.** That row (resolved) asks whether `pull_request` check runs attach at all; attachment demonstrably works here — four required workflows fired on my head in the same read. The overlap is shared CI vocabulary, which the tool states it cannot distinguish from meaning. Re-filed with `similar_ok=True` and the distinction written into the row itself.

### Landing
`hold`, Tier-1. A one-row backlog append would ordinarily self-land safely and I am not claiming otherwise — I am declining to arm auto-merge as the lane shuts down, because arming means landing unattended while nobody here is watching. Merge it whenever convenient; nothing depends on it.
